texts.error.7z_coders: this .7z was packed with a chain of coders (a filter such as BCJ2 in front of the compressor). Decoding one needs several streams advanced in lockstep, with the intermediates held somewhere, and the sandbox has nowhere to hold them. Repack with `7z a -m0=lzma2 -mf=off`, or as a .zip, and it will be read where it lies
texts.error.7z_header_unreadable: the archive header could not be read
texts.error.7z_method: this .7z uses compression method %1, which this core cannot decode. Repack with `7z a -m0=lzma2`, or as a .zip
texts.error.7z_no_memory: there was not enough memory to read the archive header
texts.error.7z_solid: That .7z is solid, which 7-Zip does by default, and a solid archive cannot be read at any useful speed: the files share one compressed stream, so reaching one means decoding everything packed before it. On a real disc dump that is minutes for the first file the emulator asks for and minutes again for each one it asks for out of order. Repack it with `7z a -ms=off <name>.7z <disc folder>` (one block per file, seekable), or as a .zip, and the core reads it where it lies.
texts.error.7z_unsupported: this .7z uses something this core cannot read (encryption, most likely)
texts.error.archive_directory: the archive's central directory cannot be read
texts.error.archive_directory_range: the archive's central directory is out of range
texts.error.archive_method: the archive uses a compression method this core cannot read (entry %1)
texts.error.archive_no_end: the end of the archive cannot be read
texts.error.archive_not_zip: it is not a zip archive (it has no end-of-central-directory record)
texts.error.disc_content: The content this disc installs onto the console could not be installed: %1.
texts.error.dkey_not_opened: The disc key cannot be opened: %1
texts.error.eboot_alone: EBOOT.BIN, and no disc. This executable is one file of a PlayStation 3 disc, and its data, its libraries and its modules are the rest of that disc; alone it boots and then waits forever. Give the core the whole disc instead: either a single .iso image, or the dumped folder packed into one .zip or .7z, which is read without being unpacked.
texts.error.firmware_no_dev_flash: The firmware file has no dev_flash packages.
texts.error.firmware_no_packages: The firmware file has no installation packages.
texts.error.firmware_not_opened: The firmware file %1 cannot be opened.
texts.error.firmware_not_pup: The firmware file is not a valid PUP: %1
texts.error.firmware_package_encrypted: A firmware package could not be decrypted: %1
texts.error.firmware_package_not_extracted: A firmware package could not be extracted: %1
texts.error.needs_dkey: This disc image is a Redump image: its filesystem is in the clear, but the disc's data is encrypted, and the game's executable reads as noise without the key. Give the image's disc key (the .dkey or .key file distributed beside it) in the Disc key slot, or use an already decrypted image.
texts.error.needs_firmware: A PS3 disc needs the system software (PS3UPDAT.PUP), and none was provided.
texts.error.needs_rap: That game's package is licensed content, and the project carries no licence for it. Its header says REQUIRE_LICENSE: the executable inside is NPDRM-encrypted, and the key is the account's own .rap file, named after the content (UP9000-NPUA80134_00-ECHOCHROME000000.rap and the like). Put that .rap in the Licence slot beside the package, and the machine decrypts and boots it.
texts.error.no_avx2: The PPU Decoder setting is 'llvm', whose compiled code needs a processor with AVX2 (x86-64-v3), and this one has none: choose 'interpreter' for this project.
texts.error.no_disc_in_archive: That archive holds no PlayStation 3 disc: nothing in it is named PS3_DISC.SFB. A disc dumped as a folder has PS3_DISC.SFB beside a PS3_GAME directory, and the archive should hold that folder or its contents.
texts.error.no_eboot: That archive has a PS3_DISC.SFB but no PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN beside it, so there is no game in it to boot.
texts.error.no_firmware: The PS3 firmware is missing, and the game needs it.
texts.error.no_vulkan: The Renderer setting is 'vulkan-hw', and this Chimera handed the core no Vulkan device. It needs a graphics driver with Vulkan and Chimera's Development build 4ca6e302 or later. Set Renderer to 'opengl-hw' to run without it.
texts.error.not_a_package: That file is not a PS3 package: %1
texts.error.not_package: The file is not a PS3 package: %1
texts.error.not_ready: The boot did not reach the ready state (state %1).
texts.error.package_not_installed: a package could not be installed (the log says which file)
texts.error.package_version: a package wants the game at version %1 (it is %2): it is a patch for another version
texts.error.pkg_content: That .pkg is not a game: installing it produced no USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN, so what it carries is content for a game (downloadable content, a licence, a theme), and there is nothing in it to boot. Put it in the Packages slot beside the game it belongs to, and put the game itself in the Game slot.
texts.error.pkg_disc_patch: That .pkg is a patch for a disc game (its PARAM.SFO says CATEGORY=GD, title %1), not a game of its own: it replaces part of a game whose disc has to be in the drive. Put the disc image in the Game slot and this package in the Packages slot, and the machine boots the patched game.
texts.error.pkg_update: That .pkg is an update, not a game: its header carries the PATCH flag, so what it holds is the files that change in a version of a game, not the game. Installed on its own it leaves a console with part of a title on it. Put the full package in the Game slot and this one in the Packages slot, and the machine boots the updated game.
texts.error.rar: A .rar archive cannot be read by this core. Reading one means carrying a RAR decoder, and the obvious one, unRAR, has a licence that does not sit with this core's terms, so no build of it can ship one. Repack the disc folder as a .zip or a .7z and it will be read without unpacking.
texts.error.save_empty: The save data zip holds no files.
texts.error.save_not_ps3: The save data holds '%1', which is not PS3 save data (every entry is savedata/<save>/<file>, as Export Save Data writes them).
texts.error.save_not_unpacked: The save data's '%1' could not be unpacked.
texts.error.save_not_zip: The save data could not be read as a zip: %1
texts.error.wrong_dkey: This disc image is still encrypted with the disc key given: the image's data does not decrypt with it, so the key belongs to another disc. A Redump image's key is the .dkey distributed beside that exact image.
texts.firmware.ps3updat_pup.about: Sony's PS3 system software update, PS3UPDAT.PUP, the file Sony distributes for the console (version 4.80 or newer). The machine decrypts it into its internal storage when it starts, before the first frame, which is how a console holds its system software. The system libraries that games use come from it. Homebrew that uses only the system's basic calls starts without it. Every real game needs it, whether it is on a disc or sold only as a download. Two projects with different versions are different machines and cannot share movies.
texts.setting.accurateppu128reservations.about: How long a loop on a 128-byte PPU memory reservation may be and still be made exact. 0 means never and -1 means always (the wiki's 'Always Enabled'). It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.accuratersxreservationaccess.abo: Makes the RSX (the graphics chip) respect the Cell processor's memory reservations exactly when it reads and writes shared memory. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.accuratespudma.about: Makes every SPU memory transfer (DMA) exactly as indivisible as it is on the hardware. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.allowhostgpulabels.about: Lets your graphics card signal the RSX's semaphores directly, instead of through RPCS3's own synchronisation. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.anisotropicfilter.about: Overrides the game's anisotropic filtering. 'Auto' keeps the game's own. It changes what your graphics card draws, not what the console calculates. Without a renderer on a graphics card it does nothing.
texts.setting.antialiasing.about: Whether the render targets a game asks to be multisampled really are. 'Disabled' draws them without multisampling, which some games need to show anything at all. It changes what your graphics card draws, not what the console calculates. Without a renderer on a graphics card it does nothing.
texts.setting.debugconsolemode.about: Makes the console a debug unit, with the larger memory that model has, for games that need it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.defaultresolution.about: The video mode the console reports to the game as the mode of its display. A game chooses its own rendering resolution from it, so it changes what the game does and not only what is shown. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.delayoddmfccommands.about: Delays every second SPU memory transfer (DMA) command so that the commands finish out of order, which some games depend on. RPCS3 chooses the order from the processor's time-stamp counter. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.disablespugetllarspinoptimizatio: Stops RPCS3 from taking a shortcut for SPUs that wait in a loop on a memory reservation. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.disablevertexcache.about: Stops RPCS3 from reusing vertex data it has already sent to the graphics card. It is for games that change that data in place. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.disablezcullqueries.about: Answers every occlusion query (the question whether something is visible) with yes, without asking the graphics card. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.driverwakeupdelay.about: How many microseconds the RSX thread waits before it wakes up to process new commands. It is for games that depend on the exact timing of their own command stream. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.emulatespecialdepthcomparison.ab: Reproduces the RSX's depth comparison where it differs from the graphics card's. It is for shadows and decals that flicker or disappear. It changes what your graphics card draws, not what the console calculates. Without a renderer on a graphics card it does nothing.
texts.setting.firmwarelibraries.about: System libraries to run from the PS3 system software (LLE) instead of RPCS3's own versions (HLE), separated by commas, for example 'libvdec.sprx'. The RPCS3 wiki names a library when RPCS3's version of it is not good enough for a game. libvdec.sprx is the video decoder. This needs the system software. Without it there is nothing to run the libraries from, and the setting is ignored. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.forcecpublit.about: Does the RSX's image copies on the processor, into the console's memory, instead of on the graphics card. It is for games that read the result back. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.framelimit.about: How RPCS3 times flips, the moments a finished picture is shown. 'PS3 Native' holds a flip that waits for vertical sync until the console's next vertical blank, as the hardware does. A rate (60, Auto and so on) holds a flip that comes early until its turn in the same way, and the RSX (the graphics chip) keeps reading commands in the meantime. RPCS3 itself pauses the RSX thread there. In this core that pause is the machine's own time, and it stopped Mortal Kombat (chimera#125) and made Rayman Legends run out of memory (chimera#165). 'Off' and 'Infinite' flip immediately. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.handlersxmemorytiling.about: Emulates the RSX's tiled memory layout when the Cell processor reads or writes a tiled region. It is for games that draw from or into such a region directly. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.lodbiasoffset.about: A number added to every texture's level-of-detail bias. Negative is sharper and positive is blurrier. It changes what your graphics card draws, not what the console calculates. Without a renderer on a graphics card it does nothing.
texts.setting.maxspursthreads.about: The largest number of SPU threads a SPURS task group may run at once. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.multithreadedrsx.about: Moves part of the work of the RSX (the graphics chip) to another thread. That thread is scheduled like every other thread in the machine, and the order in which the two finish can differ. This core fixes it so that a movie gives the same result every time, and the default is that fixed value. Chimera decides when each frame runs, so changing it is an experiment, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.port1.about: What is plugged into controller port 1. 'dualshock3' is the DualShock 3 that every PS3 was sold with, and it is what a game is told about when it asks the console for its controllers. 'none' is an empty port. It is part of the machine. A game asks which controllers are connected, and many games change their menus or their number of players by the answer. Two projects that differ here are different machines and cannot share movies.
texts.setting.port2.about: What is plugged into controller port 2. 'dualshock3' is the DualShock 3 that every PS3 was sold with, and it is what a game is told about when it asks the console for its controllers. 'none' is an empty port. It is part of the machine. A game asks which controllers are connected, and many games change their menus or their number of players by the answer. Two projects that differ here are different machines and cannot share movies.

A game asks which controllers are connected, and many games change their menus or their number of players by the answer. Two projects that differ here are different machines and cannot share movies.
texts.setting.ppu_decoder.about: How the code of the main processor (PPU) is run. 'llvm' is RPCS3's LLVM recompiler, the default: a module is compiled the first time it loads (about ten seconds for the system software's liblv2, and minutes for a big game with its libraries) and kept in the compile cache, so later sessions start warm, and compiled code runs many times faster. It counts the machine's time per basic block. 'interpreter' counts it per instruction. Both give the same result every time, but their clocks run slightly differently, so a movie plays back only with the decoder it was recorded with. A project records its decoder: one made while the interpreter was the default (before 2026-10-19) keeps it. The recompiler's code needs a processor with AVX2 (x86-64-v3); on one without it the core says so and 'interpreter' must be chosen.
texts.setting.pputhreads.about: How many PPU threads may run at once. The console has two hardware threads. This core fixes it so that a movie gives the same result every time, and the default is that fixed value. Chimera decides when each frame runs, so changing it is an experiment, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.preferredsputhreads.about: How many SPU threads may run heavy work at the same time. 0 leaves it to RPCS3. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.readcolorbuffers.about: The opposite direction of 'Write color buffers to memory'. Before drawing over a buffer, the RSX (the graphics chip) loads what the console's memory already holds for it, as the console does. A game that draws on top of a buffer it filled earlier in another way needs this, and without it that earlier content is missing. It is off by default, as in RPCS3 itself, for the same reason as the write setting: most games never do this, and the copy takes time. This is not only a display option, because the pixels it brings in were drawn by the game and the game can use them. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.readdepthbuffer.about: Before drawing into a depth buffer, loads what the console's memory already holds for it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.renderer.about:
Which renderer draws the picture. Both draw on your computer's graphics card, outside the sandbox. 'vulkan-hw' is RPCS3's Vulkan renderer and the default, as it is RPCS3's own. It needs a graphics driver that has Vulkan and a Chimera that hands Vulkan to cores (Development build 4ca6e302 or later); without either the project does not start and says why, and 'opengl-hw' is the one to choose. 'opengl-hw' is RPCS3's OpenGL renderer.

The graphics card is outside the core and is different on every computer. Pictures that a game reads back from the renderer end up in the game's memory, and the two renderers do not round every pixel alike. A different renderer, or a different graphics driver, can therefore give a slightly different machine: a movie recorded with one plays back only with the same one. Choose the renderer when you create the project. On a computer that offers neither OpenGL nor Vulkan, the core draws nothing and says so.
texts.setting.resolutionscale.about: Draws at this percentage of the game's own resolution. The picture Chimera receives changes size with it. It changes what your graphics card draws, not what the console calculates. Without a renderer on a graphics card it does nothing.
texts.setting.resolutionscalethreshold.about: Render targets (the surfaces a game draws into) smaller than this many pixels on each side are never scaled by 'Resolution scale'. The RPCS3 wiki writes the value in the form '320x320'. Here it is just the one number. It changes what your graphics card draws, not what the console calculates. Without a renderer on a graphics card it does nothing.
texts.setting.rsxfifoaccuracy.about: How the RSX reads the command stream that the Cell processor writes. The stricter modes see each command exactly as and when the console's chip would. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.shadermode.about: How the shaders for your graphics card are made. This core compiles each shader on the RSX thread before drawing with it. The asynchronous modes draw without a shader until one is ready, so what is drawn depends on how fast your computer compiles. It changes what your graphics card draws, not what the console calculates. Without a renderer on a graphics card it does nothing. This core fixes it so that a movie gives the same result every time, and the default is that fixed value. Chimera decides when each frame runs, so changing it is an experiment, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.shaderquality.about: The floating point precision used by the shaders on your graphics card. It changes what your graphics card draws, not what the console calculates. Without a renderer on a graphics card it does nothing.
texts.setting.sleeptimersaccuracy.about: How precisely the console's sleep and timer calls are followed. The finer choices wake threads exactly on time and are slower. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.spu_decoder.about: How the code of the SPU processors is run. 'asmjit' is RPCS3's ASMJIT recompiler. It gives the same results several times faster, and it counts the machine's time once per loop pass and function entry. 'interpreter' counts time per instruction. Both give the same result every time, but their clocks run slightly differently, so a movie plays back only with the decoder it was recorded with.
texts.setting.spublocksize.about: How much SPU code the recompiler compiles as one unit. Larger blocks are faster. They also change the points where the recompiler counts time (once per function and loop), so the machine's clock runs slightly differently. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.spuloopdetection.about: Detects SPUs that wait in a loop and lets another thread run. This core fixes it so that a movie gives the same result every time, and the default is that fixed value. Chimera decides when each frame runs, so changing it is an experiment, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.spuxfloataccuracy.about: How exactly the SPU processors' non-standard floating point is reproduced. Choose 'Accurate' for games whose physics or animation go wrong. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.strictrenderingmode.about: Follows the rules of the RSX (the graphics chip) exactly where RPCS3 normally takes faster shortcuts. It is slower, and it is correct for games that the shortcuts break. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.vblankntscfixup.about: Makes the vblank rate 59.94 instead of 60, as on an NTSC console. This core fixes it so that a movie gives the same result every time, and the default is that fixed value. Chimera decides when each frame runs, so changing it is an experiment, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.vblankrate.about: How many vertical blank (vblank) events the console sees each second. Games that time themselves by vblank run faster at a higher rate, and some run correctly only at 120. This core fixes it so that a movie gives the same result every time, and the default is that fixed value. Chimera decides when each frame runs, so changing it is an experiment, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.writecolorbuffers.about: The RSX (the PS3's graphics chip) draws into buffers that are also in the console's memory, and on a real PS3 a game can read them back at any time. This setting makes the renderer write every finished color buffer back into that memory, as the console does. It is off by default, as in RPCS3 itself. Most games never read their own picture, and copying every buffer back on every frame is expensive. With it on, Resident Evil 5 ran out of memory (16 GiB) within thirty frames, and with it off the game runs. Turn it on for a game that reads the screen back. The sign of such a game is a picture, made by the game from its own screen, that comes out black or out of date. Oblivion draws the thumbnail of a saved game this way, and without this setting the icon is black in the exported save and in the game's own load menu. This is not only a display option, because a game that reads those pixels can act on them. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.writedepthbuffer.about: Writes finished depth buffers back into the console's memory, where a game that reads them expects them. It is the depth version of 'Write color buffers to memory'. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.zcullaccuracy.about: How exactly the counts of visible pixels (the ZCULL statistics of the RSX, the PS3's graphics chip) are reported back to the game. 'Precise' counts every sample and waits for the graphics card. 'Approximate' and 'Relaxed' answer sooner with a less exact count. Some games need that to run at all, and some draw wrongly with it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.slot.dkey.help: The 32-character disc key that decrypts a Redump PS3 image (the .dkey file distributed with it). It is not needed for a decrypted image or a homebrew executable. A package game does not need one either, because a .pkg contains no encrypted disc.
texts.slot.game.help: The game. It is one of four things. (1) A PS3 executable (.elf, .self), started directly as a modified console would start it. (2) A disc image (.iso). This is either a decrypted image, or a Redump image with its disc key given under Disc key. (3) A disc copied as a FOLDER and packed into a single .zip or .7z. The archive is read in place and never unpacked, so it may be as large as the disc. Store the files in it without compression, so that the game's big files can be read at any position. A disc game's EBOOT.BIN alone is not enough, because the game's data is in the rest of the disc. A .7z works the same way, but it must be packed NON-SOLID: `7z a -ms=off`. By default 7-Zip packs all files into one shared stream, which has to be decoded from its start to reach anything in it. Reading the first 64 KB of one disc's EBOOT.BIN took 190 seconds that way. A solid archive is therefore refused, so that it cannot look as if the program has stopped responding. (4) The .pkg of a title sold only as a download and never on a disc. It is installed on the console's hard disk before the machine starts, exactly as the console's own menu (XMB) installs it, and the machine starts what the installation produced. No disc and no disc key are involved. A package that is content FOR a game (downloadable content, a licence, a patch for a disc game) is refused here by name. It belongs under Packages.
texts.slot.pkg.help: PS3 package files (.pkg) that are installed on the console's hard disk before the machine starts, the way the console's own menu (XMB) installs them: downloadable content, game patches and unlock packages. Any number can be given, and they are installed in the order listed. Encrypted content (EDAT) also needs its licence. A .rap licence comes as a package of its own, and a package that was repacked to need no licence installs and works alone. The project and the movie record exactly which packages they were, so a movie that plays a game with its downloadable content can be played back by anyone who has the same files. A file that is not a PS3 package, or a patch for another version of the game, is refused, so that content is never silently missing.
texts.slot.rap.help: The account licence (.rap) for a PlayStation Store title that was paid for. A purchased package is protected (NPDRM): its executable and its data are encrypted, and the key is this 16-byte file. The console keeps it in the user's exdata folder and looks it up BY NAME, so the file's name is the content id and must not be changed. Give one for each package that needs it, and the machine decrypts and starts what it unlocks. Without it a licensed game stops at 'failed to decrypt content'. A free package (a demo, or a repack that needs no licence) needs none. The project and the movie record exactly which file it was, as they do for every other file the machine starts with.
texts.slot.rap.name_help: A .rap file is named after the content it unlocks, and the console finds it by that name, for example UP9000-NPUA80134_00-ECHOCHROME000000.rap. If it is renamed the console cannot find it, so give it exactly as you got it.
texts.slot.savedata.help: The saved games the console starts with. This is the zip that Emulator > Export Save Data... writes, given back unchanged. It holds the user's savedata folder, with one directory per save (BLUS30007-SAVE-..., with PARAM.SFO, icons and the game's own files). It is unpacked onto the console's hard disk before the machine starts, so a run can continue where another stopped. The file is never changed. The project and the movie record exactly which file it was, so a movie that starts from a saved game can be played back by anyone who has the same file. Leave it empty and the console has no saves. A zip that holds anything else is refused.

texts.suggest.no_title_id: RPCS3 compatibility: this game carries no title id, so it cannot be looked up.
